desc:
AI content drafting with review steps gives your team a faster way to produce product text, blog posts, emails and social captions in your own voice. Ecom Swift LLC builds the drafting set-up, the voice guide and the approval step, so a person always signs off before anything is published.

## What is AI content drafting with review steps?

It is a set-up where an AI model writes a first draft from your instructions, and a named person checks it before it goes anywhere public. The model does the slow part, which is getting words onto the page. Your editors keep the part that needs judgment: facts, tone and what the business is willing to say.

The review step is what separates a useful tool from a risky one. Without it, drafts drift in tone and sometimes state things that are not true about your products.

## Why drafting without a plan goes wrong

Most teams start by pasting a request into a chat window. The first result looks fine, the second sounds like a different company, and the tenth contains a claim nobody approved. Nothing is saved or repeatable.

A proper set-up writes your rules down once. Voice, vocabulary, forbidden claims and format all live in a template that every draft starts from. New staff get the same results as your most experienced writer.

## How it affects your results

Drafting changes how much time your team spends on routine writing. A product description, a restock email or a caption set takes minutes to review instead of an hour to write from nothing. That time moves to the work that earns attention: better offers, better photos, replies to customers.

Consistency matters as much as speed. Shoppers and readers notice when a brand sounds the same across its store, newsletter and social posts. Because the template carries your voice, new pages match older ones. Quality still depends on your inputs, so the result varies with how good your samples and facts are.

## What a good drafting set-up includes

- A voice guide built from real copy you like, covering tone, sentence length and words you prefer.
- A reusable instruction template for each content type, such as product text or a newsletter.
- A list of banned phrases, banned claims and topics that need legal or owner approval.
- Fact fields, so the draft is built from your product data rather than guesses.
- A review checklist that tells editors exactly what to verify.
- A form, spreadsheet or in-site screen where staff request drafts without writing instructions.
- A review queue where drafts wait as drafts until someone approves them.
- Saved versions, so you can compare an edit with the original draft.
- Fact-check prompts that flag numbers, names and promises for a human to confirm.

## What we do

We start with your samples. You send a few pieces of copy you are proud of and a few you dislike, and we turn the difference into a written voice guide. From that we build the instruction templates and the banned list, then test them on real items from your catalog or calendar.

The Basic package covers one content type with a template and review checklist. The Standard package adds more content types, a form that creates drafts in one click and a review queue. The Premium package connects drafting to your site or spreadsheet, supports bulk runs, keeps version history and ends with a handover call for your editors. We tune the wording with you until the drafts need light edits rather than rewrites.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Share samples of your best existing copy, not only a description of your style.
- Give every draft real facts to work from, such as materials, sizes and policies.
- Name one person who owns final approval for each content type.
- Keep the banned list short, clear and updated when something goes wrong.
- Read every draft in full before publishing, even when it looks polished.

**Avoid:**
- Publishing drafts directly with no human review.
- Asking the tool to invent customer reviews, quotes or personal stories.
- Making claims about health, safety or results that you cannot support.
- Using the same instructions for every content type.
- Treating the first draft as finished copy.

## Who it is for

A small online shop with a growing catalog needs product text in a consistent voice and has no full-time writer. A marketing manager sends weekly emails and social captions and wants a first draft ready on Monday morning. A content team running a blog wants outlines and first drafts that editors then rewrite and fact-check.

## What we need from you

Send a few samples of copy you like, a list of what you want drafted, your product or topic facts and any words or claims that are off limits. If drafts will connect to your site or spreadsheet, we ask to be added as a collaborator, staff or team user where the platform supports it. We never need your passwords, and your own accounts stay yours throughout. After you order, we reply with a short checklist and keep you updated until handover.
